claim: The role of cerebellum in controlling eye movements is well established.
source_text: The role of cerebellum in controlling eye movements is well established
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations (Inoshita and Hirano, 2018; Ivry and Diener, 1991; Kunimatsu et al., 2016) and represents established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: The cerebellum participates in more complex cognitive visual functions.
source_text: over the last few decades evidence is emerging that the cerebellum also participates in more complex cognitive visual functions
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Baier et al., 2010; Brissenden et al., 2016; Courchesne et al., 1994; Nicolson et al., 2001; Voogd et al., 2012) indicating emerging evidence from the literature.

claim: The cerebellum uses visual information to guide the planning of saccades while interacting with areas such as the frontal eye fields, lateral intraparietal area, superior colliculus, and basal ganglia.
source_text: while interacting with areas such as the frontal eye fields (FEFs), lateral intraparietal area, superior colliculus, and basal ganglia, the cerebellum uses visual information to guide the planning of saccades
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Gao et al., 2018; Kunimatsu et al., 2018; Scerra et al., 2019; Tanaka, 2006; Wardak et al., 2011).

claim: Single-unit DN neurons modulated spiking activity over the entire time course of the task in a heterogeneous manner.
source_text: We found that single-unit DN neurons modulated spiking activity over the entire time course of the task, and that their activity often bridged temporally separated intra-trial events, yet in a heterogeneous manner.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the experimental recordings of DN neurons during the task, supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both NHPs showed different behavioral strategies, which influenced the performance.
source_text: Both NHPs showed different behavioral strategies, which influenced the performance.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is based on behavioral analysis and modeling of the two animals' performance data during the task.

claim: Activity of the DN neurons reflected the unique strategies of the two NHPs.
source_text: Activity of the DN neurons reflected the unique strategies
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on analysis of neural recordings correlated with behavioral strategies, involving both direct data and inference about the relationship.

claim: The direction of the visual stimulus was frequently encoded long before an upcoming saccade.
source_text: with the direction of the visual stimulus frequently being encoded long before an upcoming saccade
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the encoding model analysis of neural activity relative to task events.

claim: The latency of the ramping activity of DN neurons following presentation of the visual stimulus was shorter in the better performing NHP.
source_text: the latency of the ramping activity of DN neurons following presentation of the visual stimulus was shorter in the better performing NHP
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis of neural ramping activity comparing the two animals.

claim: DN neurons predominantly receive inputs from Purkinje cells in the D1 and D2 zones of the lateral cerebellum as well as neurons of the principal olive and medial pons.
source_text: Labeling with the retrograde tracer Cholera Toxin B in the recording location in the DN indicated that these neurons predominantly receive inputs from Purkinje cells in the D1 and D2 zones of the lateral cerebellum as well as neurons of the principal olive and medial pons
evidence_reasoning: This is based on anatomical tracing data using CTb injections and subsequent histological analysis.

claim: The D1 and D2 zones and their connected regions are known to connect with neurons in the prefrontal cortex contributing to planning of saccades.
source_text: all regions known to connect with neurons in the prefrontal cortex contributing to planning of saccades
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws on established anatomical knowledge from the literature about cerebellar-cortical connections.

claim: DN neurons can dynamically modulate their activity during a visual attention task, comprising not only sensorimotor but also cognitive attentional components.
source_text: our results highlight that DN neurons can dynamically modulate their activity during a visual attention task, comprising not only sensorimotor but also cognitive attentional components
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing neural modulation during different task components.

claim: Mo consistently outperformed Mi in task performance.
source_text: Mo consistently outperformed Mi, and this trend was present across different experimental sessions
evidence_reasoning: This is based on behavioral performance data collected across multiple sessions (Figure 1C, D).

claim: The performance differences between monkeys do not directly represent the structure of the initial learning process.
source_text: the performance differences do not directly represent the structure of the initial learning process
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the fact that analysis used data from periods after monkeys had been sufficiently trained.

claim: Mi's overall performance increase was mostly mediated by his improvement in the subset of up-/downward trials in the task.
source_text: his overall performance increase was mostly mediated by his improvement in the subset of up-/downward trials in the task
evidence_reasoning: This finding is based on logistic regression modeling of behavioral data showing differential weighting of U/D vs L/R trials.

claim: Mo exhibited increased weighting of the stimulus in both U/D and L/R trials.
source_text: Mo, on the other hand, exhibited increased weighting of the stimulus in both U/D and L/R trials
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the logistic regression model applied to Mo's behavioral data.

claim: Mi assigned less weight to the previous saccade over time if the current trial was in the L/R direction.
source_text: Mi assigned less weight to the previous saccade over time if the current trial was in the L/R direction (p = 0.016; R2 = 0.32
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistically significant finding from the past-trial analysis with specific p-value and R-squared reported.

claim: There was no change in event weight to predict the response on the current trial in the past-trial variables for Mo.
source_text: there was no change in event weight to predict the response on the current trial in the past-trial variables for Mo
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative finding from the statistical analysis of Mo's behavioral data.

claim: 305 DN neurons were recorded while the animals performed the Landolt C task.
source_text: Single-unit activity was recorded for 305 DN neurons, while the animals performed the Landolt C task
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement of the sample size from the experimental recordings.

claim: The activity levels of DN neurons in both Mi and Mo changed during the instruction and movement stage, depending on the stimulus identity.
source_text: The activity levels of DN neurons in both Mi and Mo changed during the instruction and movement stage, depending on the stimulus identity
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the analysis of neural recordings during different task phases.

claim: The population of suppressing neurons exhibited modulation significantly earlier than facilitating units after C-stimulus onset.
source_text: the population of suppressing neurons (n = 85) exhibited the modulation significantly earlier (p < 0.0041; Kolmogorov–Smirnov test) than did the facilitating units (n = 90)
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistically significant finding with specific p-value and statistical test reported.

claim: There was no significant difference in timing between facilitating and suppressing cells during the saccade window.
source_text: This was not the case (p = 0.23) for facilitating (n = 57) and suppressing (n = 38) cells during the saccade window
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative finding with specific p-value reported from statistical comparison.

claim: Many DN cells modulated their activity in relation to more than one task event.
source_text: Many DN cells modulated their activity in relation to more than one task event
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the GLM analysis of neural responses to multiple task events.

claim: Many cells encoded the gap direction, the saccade or both, while a smaller fraction was sensitive to the events in the previous trial.
source_text: We found that many cells encoded the gap direction, the saccade or both, while a smaller fraction was sensitive to the events in the previous trial
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the GLM encoding model analysis showing which task variables were encoded.

claim: Many units showed firing rate modulation in relation to both particular gap directions and saccades.
source_text: Many units showed firing rate modulation in relation to both particular gap directions and saccades
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the encoding analysis showing multimodal responses.

claim: Neural response after the saccade in trials where the animal made a mistake was a common feature.
source_text: a neural response after the saccade in trials where the animal made a mistake was a common feature
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the neural recordings during error trials.

claim: These error-related responses are possibly related to the absence of reward.
source_text: it is possible that these responses are related to the absence of reward
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the error-related responses, supported by citations to related work (Heffley and Hull, 2019; Kostadinov et al., 2019).

claim: The fractions of recorded neurons that were sensitive to particular task parameters were similar in both animals.
source_text: the fractions of recorded neurons that were sensitive to particular task parameters, including gap direction, saccade direction, or miscellaneous were similar in both animals
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from the encoding analysis between the two animals.

claim: The similar fractions indicate that comparable populations of DN neurons were sampled in the two NHPs.
source_text: indicating that we sampled from comparable populations of DN neurons in the two NHPs
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the similarity in neural population characteristics between animals.

claim: The latency from the onset of the C-stimulus to the moment of ramping in Mo was on average 115 ms shorter than that of Mi.
source_text: the latency from the onset of the C-stimulus to the moment of ramping in Mo was on average 115 ms shorter (F = 10.9, p = 0.001) than that of Mi
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding with specific statistical values from the ramping analysis.

claim: The trial outcome (whether the monkey made a correct or incorrect choice) was the condition that was most reliably represented in neural activity.
source_text: The condition that was most reliably represented was the trial outcome, that is, whether the monkey made a correct or incorrect choice
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the decoding model analysis showing which variables could be predicted from neural activity.

claim: The proportion of cells from which the trial outcome could be decoded increased at about 1 s following the presentation of the C-stimulus and persisted throughout the delay period.
source_text: The proportion of cells from which the trial outcome could be decoded increased at about 1 s following the presentation of the C-stimulus to the monkey, and this persisted throughout the delay period and remained present for more than a second after the monkey had made his choice
evidence_reasoning: This is a temporal finding from the decoding analysis showing when outcome information was present.

claim: Mi had more cells from which the trial outcome could be decoded around the time of the reward compared to Mo.
source_text: Compared to Mo, Mi had more cells from which the trial outcome could be decoded around the time of the reward
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from the decoding analysis between the two animals.

claim: Mo showed many cells in which information about the C-stimulus, including the gap direction, could be decoded.
source_text: Mo showed many cells in which we could decode information about the C-stimulus, including the gap direction, which is relevant to making a correct choice
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the decoding analysis specific to Mo's neural population.

claim: Mo's DN activity was generally better entrained to the stimulus, leading to better overall behavioral performance.
source_text: Possibly, this was particularly visible in Mo as his DN activity was generally better entrained to the stimulus, leading to a better overall behavioral performance
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference connecting the neural encoding findings to behavioral performance differences.

claim: Mi had more cells than Mo that maintained information about the choice he had made in the previous trial.
source_text: Mi instead had more cells than Mo that maintained information about the choice he had made in the previous trial, well into the time-frame of the ongoing trial
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from the decoding analysis of past-trial information.

claim: There were almost no cells from which the gap direction of the past trial could be decoded in either NHP.
source_text: there were almost no cells from which the gap direction of the past trial could be decoded in either NHP
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative finding from the decoding analysis of past-trial gap direction.

claim: The CTb injections were focused on the centrolateral part of the DN positioned in the center of its rostrocaudal axis.
source_text: the injections were focused on the centrolateral part of the DN positioned in the center of its rostrocaudal axis
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the anatomical location of tracer injections based on post-mortem analysis.

claim: The functionally relevant recording area covered a vertical column of approximately 2 mm long, 2 mm wide, and 3 mm deep.
source_text: we estimated that the functionally relevant recording area covered a vertical column of approximately 2 mm long, 2 mm wide, and 3 mm deep
evidence_reasoning: This is an estimate based on the distribution of modulating cells according to stereotactic coordinates and recording depths.

claim: The size of the injection was bigger in Mo as compared to Mi.
source_text: the size of the injection was bigger in Mo as compared to Mi, possibly reflecting different stock preparations or anisotropic spread of the tracer
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the anatomical analysis with speculative reasoning about the cause.

claim: Mo showed more labeled cells in the inferior olive than Mi.
source_text: when we quantified the number of retrogradely labeled neurons in one out of four sections of the inferior olive (IO), so as to assess the relative effective size of the DN injections in both animals, we found more labeled cells in Mo
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the anatomical tracing analysis.

claim: In Mi, the dorsolateral and ventrolateral leaf of the principal olivary nucleus contained 38 and 78 cells, respectively, while the ventrolateral outgrowth contained only 4 cells.
source_text: In Mi the dorsolateral and ventrolateral leaf of the principal olivary nucleus (PO) contained 38 and 78 cells, respectively, while the ventrolateral outgrowth of the PO contained only 4 cells
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from cell counting in anatomical sections.

claim: In Mo, 1977, 763 and 312 neurons were counted in the dorsolateral leaf, ventrolateral leaf, and ventrolateral outgrowth of the PO, respectively.
source_text: in Mo we counted 1977, 763 and 312 neurons in the dorsolateral leaf, ventrolateral leaf, and ventrolateral outgrowth of the PO, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from cell counting in anatomical sections.

claim: The labeling in the PO of the IO was in line with the retrograde labeling in the pons, which was predominantly confined to the medial pontine nuclei in both Mi and Mo.
source_text: The labeling in the PO of the IO was in line with the retrograde labeling in the pons, which was predominantly confined to the medial pontine nuclei in both Mi and Mo, with Mo showing more labeled cells
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the anatomical tracing showing consistent patterns across brain regions.

claim: Mo showed more retrogradely labeled Purkinje cells (n = 1314) than Mi (n = 84).
source_text: Mo showed more retrogradely labeled Purkinje cells (n = 1314) than Mi (n = 84), when we screened 1 out of 24 sections of the cerebellar cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from counting labeled Purkinje cells in cerebellar sections.

claim: Most of the labeled PCs appeared to be located in the D1 and D2 zones of the cerebellar cortex.
source_text: Most of the labeled PCs appeared to be located in the D1 and D2 zones of the cerebellar cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the anatomical analysis with reference to established zonal nomenclature (Voogd et al., 2012).

claim: The CTb injections into the DN provided anterograde labeling of the climbing fibers.
source_text: the CTb injections into the DN also provided anterograde labeling of the climbing fibers
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the anatomical tracing showing anterograde transport of the tracer.

claim: The distribution of anterograde climbing fiber labeling overlapped to a large extent with that of the retrograde labeling of the PCs in both Mi and Mo.
source_text: the distribution of which overlapped to a large extent with that of the retrograde labeling of the PCs in both Mi and Mo
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from comparing the spatial distribution of different types of labeling.

claim: Anterograde CTb labeling was found in the parvocellular and magnocellular red nucleus, zona incerta and deep mesencephalic nucleus as well as various thalamic nuclei.
source_text: we found anterograde CTb labeling in the higher brainstem; this included for example the parvocellular and magnocellular red nucleus, zona incerta and deep mesencephalic nucleus as well as various thalamic nuclei, such as the ventrolateral thalamic nucleus (VL), pulvinar nucleus (Pul), mediodorsal thalamic nucleus (MD), and centromedial and centrolateral thalamic nuclei
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the anatomical tracing showing projection targets of DN neurons.

claim: No substantial labeling was found in the superior colliculus, ventral tegmental area or hypothalamus.
source_text: we did not find substantial labeling in the superior colliculus, ventral tegmental area or hypothalamus
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative finding from the anatomical tracing analysis.

claim: The labeled areas are consistent with previous studies illustrating disynaptic pathways from the DN to cerebral cortical areas involved in visual processing such as the FEF area.
source_text: The labeled areas we found are consistent with previous studies illustrating disynaptic pathways from the DN to cerebral cortical areas involved in visual processing such as the FEF area
evidence_reasoning: This statement connects the current anatomical findings to previous literature (Kipping et al., 2013; Middleton and Strick, 2001; Romanski et al., 1997).

claim: DN cells connected with the D1 and D2 zones in the cerebellar cortex have highly diverse activity patterns.
source_text: we found that DN cells connected with the D1 and D2 zones in the cerebellar cortex have highly diverse activity patterns
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary finding combining anatomical and electrophysiological data.

claim: DN cell activity often bridges different experimental epochs and frequently shows both upbound and downbound modulations.
source_text: Their activity often bridges different experimental epochs and frequently show both upbound and downbound modulations
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the neural recordings with reference to similar observations (De Zeeuw, 2021).

claim: Following training of the task, many DN neurons respond in a visual direction- or movement direction-selective manner more than half a second before the saccade of choice is made.
source_text: following training of the task, many DN neurons respond in a visual direction- or movement direction-selective manner more than half a second before the saccade of choice is made
evidence_reasoning: This is a temporal finding from the analysis of neural responses relative to behavioral events.

claim: Multimodality and timing-dependent activation appear to be common properties of neurons in the lateral cerebellum.
source_text: Thus, multimodality and timing-dependent activation appear to be common properties of neurons in the lateral cerebellum
evidence_reasoning: This is a general conclusion drawn from the patterns observed in the neural data.

claim: The region where recordings were made in the DN forms part of the cerebellar D1 and D2 microcomplex.
source_text: The distribution of the retrogradely labeled PCs in lateral lobules VII and VIII as well as crus I/II indicates that the region where we recorded in the DN forms part of the cerebellar D1 and D2 microcomplex
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on anatomical tracing data and reference to established cerebellar organization (De Zeeuw, 2021; De Zeeuw and Ten Brinke, 2015).

claim: The part of the medial pons that showed retrograde labeling is known to receive direct input from the prefrontal cortex and to activate the D zones during decision making and motor planning.
source_text: This conclusion is supported by the retrograde CTb labeling we found in the part of the medial pons that is known to receive direct input from the prefrontal cortex and to activate the D zones during decision making and motor planning
evidence_reasoning: This combines current anatomical findings with established knowledge from multiple citations about pontine connectivity and function.

claim: Most of the retrograde labeling in the olive following the injections in the DN was present in the dlPO and vlPO, which are part of the D1 and D2 modules.
source_text: most of the retrograde labeling in the olive following the injections in the DN was present in the dlPO and vlPO, which are also part of the D1 and D2 modules
evidence_reasoning: This is an anatomical finding with reference to established modular organization (Voogd et al., 2012; Voogd and Ruigrok, 2012).

claim: Most anterogradely labeled fibers were found in the pulvinar, mediodorsal thalamus and ventrolateral thalamus, which are known to connect to various parts of the prefrontal cortex.
source_text: Most anterogradely labeled fibers were found in the pulvinar, mediodorsal thalamus and ventrolateral thalamus, which are known to connect to various parts of the prefrontal cortex, such as FEF and Brodmann area 46
evidence_reasoning: This combines anatomical tracing findings with established knowledge about thalamo-cortical connections from the literature.

claim: The dorsal attention network has been shown to connect to lobules VII and VIII.
source_text: the dorsal attention network has been shown to connect to lobules VII and VIII
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous neuroimaging studies (Brissenden et al., 2016; Buckner et al., 2011).

claim: The anatomical findings suggest that the DN region under study is at least partly integrated in a functional closed loop between cerebellum and cerebral cortex that appears to be involved in decision making, planning, and attention.
source_text: the anatomical findings suggest that the DN region under study is at least partly integrated in a functional closed loop between cerebellum and cerebral cortex that appears to be involved in decision making, planning, and attention
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the anatomical connectivity patterns observed.

claim: The spatial and temporal dissociation of cue and action in the Landolt C task allows separation of neural activity related to visual and attentional processes from that related to motor coordination.
source_text: The spatial and temporal dissociation of cue and action in this task allows us to separate neural activity related to the visual and attentional processes from that related to motor coordination
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological inference about the task design with reference to similar approaches (Avila et al., 2022; Goldberg and Segraves, 1987).

claim: Individual DN cells can encode both the direction of the visual cue and the associated direction of the subsequent saccade.
source_text: Our data reveal that individual DN cells can encode both the direction of the visual cue and the associated direction of the subsequent saccade
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the encoding analysis of neural responses.

claim: Different task-specific activations in the cerebellar cortex may be relayed downstream to the same target neurons in the cerebellar nuclei.
source_text: suggesting that different task-specific activations in the cerebellar cortex may be relayed downstream to the same target neurons in the cerebellar nuclei
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about circuit mechanisms based on the multimodal encoding observed in DN neurons.

claim: The current data are compatible with and expand upon fMRI studies demonstrating that lateral lobules VIIb/VIIIa upstream of the DN exhibit functional properties characteristic of the dorsal attention network.
source_text: Our data are compatible with and expand upon fMRI studies, which have demonstrated that lateral lobules VIIb/VIIIa upstream of the DN exhibit functional properties characteristic of the dorsal attention network in the cerebral cortex
evidence_reasoning: This statement connects the current findings to previous neuroimaging literature (Brissenden et al., 2018; Brissenden et al., 2016; van Es et al., 2019).

claim: Lateral lobules VIIb/VIIIa show task-specific activation that depends on representation of visuospatial location and/or load of working memory.
source_text: this part of the cerebellar hemispheres shows task-specific activation in that their responses depend on representation of visuospatial location and/or load of working memory
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous fMRI studies (Brissenden et al., 2018; Brissenden et al., 2016; van Es et al., 2019).

claim: Injecting accelerations of simple spike modulations of PCs in the cerebellar hemispheres into the complex of cerebellar nuclei may be instrumental in improving the performance of responses to covert attention.
source_text: The difference in onset of DN ramping between the monkeys highlights the possibility that injecting accelerations of simple spike modulations of PCs in the cerebellar hemispheres into the complex of cerebellar nuclei may be instrumental in improving the performance of responses to covert attention
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the ramping differences, drawing an analogy to previous work on vestibular processing (De Zeeuw et al., 1995).

claim: The data on differences in choice performance between Mo and Mi are supported by different reaction times in expert and amateur baseball players, who show cerebellar activation upon visual presentation of a pitched ball.
source_text: our data on the differences in choice performance between Mo and Mi are also supported by the different reaction times in expert and amateur baseball players, who show cerebellar activation upon visual presentation of a pitched ball
evidence_reasoning: This connects the current findings to a related study on expertise and cerebellar function (Owens et al., 2018).

claim: The current recordings are corroborated by electrophysiological studies that have revealed a role of the cerebellar nuclei, including the DN, in motor planning.
source_text: our recordings are corroborated by electrophysiological studies that have revealed a role of the cerebellar nuclei, including that of the DN, in motor planning
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to previous electrophysiological studies (Chabrol et al., 2019; Deverett et al., 2019; Deverett et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018).

claim: The DN cells recorded in the current study may contribute to the preparation of directed saccades through their projections to the FEF via the thalamus.
source_text: The DN cells recorded in the current study may contribute to the preparation of directed saccades through their projections to the FEF via the thalamus
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about functional connectivity based on anatomical pathways described in the literature (Lindeman et al., 2021; Middleton and Strick, 2001; Romanski et al., 1997).

claim: FEF neurons that are embedded in the dorsal attention network encode multiple aspects of saccade planning and processing, including target identification in covert visual searches.
source_text: Similar to our DN neurons, the FEF neurons that are embedded in the dorsal attention network encode multiple aspects of saccade planning and processing, including target identification in covert visual searches
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies on FEF function (Brissenden et al., 2018; Brissenden et al., 2016; Buckner et al., 2011; van Es et al., 2019).

claim: FEF neurons encode decision making among multiple choices.
source_text: as well as decision making among multiple choices
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to studies on FEF and decision making (Ding and Gold, 2012; Gregoriou et al., 2012; Hanes and Schall, 1996; Monosov and Thompson, 2009; Schall and Hanes, 1993).

claim: FEF neurons can show ramping activity before upcoming eye movements.
source_text: FEF neurons can show the type of ramping activity before upcoming eye movements
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies (Basu and Murthy, 2020; Raghavan and Joshua, 2017).

claim: Ramping activity is one of the main signatures of motor preparation.
source_text: Given that such ramping activity is one of the main signatures of motor preparation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations (Chabrol et al., 2019; Deverett et al., 2019; Gao et al., 2018; Hanks et al., 2015; Svoboda and Li, 2018).

claim: DN neurons may have a critical role in facilitating the preparation of visuomotor processing in general.
source_text: DN neurons may have a critical role in facilitating the preparation of visuomotor processing in general
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the ramping activity and encoding properties observed.

claim: The cerebellum receives inputs from many different external sensory as well as internal cognitive modalities, all of which can be integrated during the preparation and execution of complex tasks.
source_text: The cerebellum receives inputs from many different external sensory as well as internal cognitive modalities, all of which can be integrated during the preparation and execution of complex tasks
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge with citation to a review (De Zeeuw, 2021).

claim: In the cerebellar cortex, integration of different modalities can take place at both the input and output stage.
source_text: In the cerebellar cortex such integration can take place at both the input and output stage
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established understanding of cerebellar circuit organization.

claim: At the input stage, activation of different sensory modalities has been shown to enhance spiking output of granule cells.
source_text: At the input stage, that is, at the level of the granule cells in the granular layer, activation of different sensory modalities has been shown to enhance spiking output
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies (Giovannucci et al., 2017; Ishikawa et al., 2015).

claim: Many individual granule cells can receive inputs from both the cuneate nucleus relaying sensory proprioceptive signals and the pontine nuclei mediating presumptive motor command signals.
source_text: given that many individual granule cells can receive inputs from both the cuneate nucleus relaying sensory proprioceptive signals and the pontine nuclei mediating presumptive motor command signals
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to anatomical and physiological studies (Guo et al., 2021; Huang et al., 2013; Wagner et al., 2019).

claim: Sensory, motor and cognitive signals can be integrated at the level of the cerebellar input layer.
source_text: it is likely that sensory, motor and cognitive signals can also be integrated at the level of the cerebellar input layer
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the convergence of different input pathways onto granule cells.

claim: At the level of PCs in the molecular layer with inputs from thousands of parallel fibers, the opportunities for convergence and integration of different modalities are even greater.
source_text: At the level of the PCs in the molecular layer with inputs from thousands of parallel fibers contacting single PC dendrites, the opportunities for convergence and integration of different modalities are even greater
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established anatomical knowledge about PC connectivity (Gao et al., 2012).

claim: Integration of various forms of sensory, motor, and/or cognitive signals occurs at the level of the DN neurons downstream of PCs in the D1 and D2 zones.
source_text: Our results demonstrate that integration of various forms of sensory, motor, and/or cognitive signals also occurs at the level of the DN neurons downstream of PCs in the D1 and D2 zones
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the multimodal encoding observed in DN neurons.

claim: Single DN neurons can encode the direction of a visual stimulus, as well as the preparation and execution of a saccadic eye movement into a particular direction.
source_text: Indeed, single DN neurons can encode the direction of a visual stimulus, as well as the preparation and execution of a saccadic eye movement into a particular direction
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the encoding analysis.

claim: The encoding of both stimulus and saccade directions is present in the biggest proportion of task-modulated neurons in both monkeys.
source_text: The encoding of both stimulus and saccade directions is present in the biggest proportion of task-modulated neurons in both monkeys
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the encoding model analysis.

claim: The electrophysiological data on DN encoding during the Landolt C task are in line with fMRI studies showing covert attention signals in the cerebellum.
source_text: Our electrophysiological data on DN encoding during the Landolt C task are in line with fMRI studies showing covert attention signals in the cerebellum
evidence_reasoning: This connects the current findings to previous neuroimaging studies (Brissenden et al., 2018; Brissenden et al., 2016; van Es et al., 2019).

claim: Neuroimaging studies point toward a coordination of cerebral and cerebellar cortical activation during covert attention.
source_text: These neuroimaging studies, which have also implemented a consistent distractor stimulus to evaluate the validity of the task, point toward a coordination of cerebral and cerebellar cortical activation during covert attention
evidence_reasoning: This is based on findings from previous neuroimaging studies with reference to the Posner paradigm (Posner, 1980).

claim: The premotor theory of covert attention has mainly highlighted the relevance of processing in the cerebral cortex.
source_text: the premotor theory of covert attention, which has so far mainly highlighted the relevance of processing in the cerebral cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is a characterization of an established theory with citations (Corbetta et al., 1998; Nobre et al., 2000; Rizzolatti et al., 1987).

claim: The premotor theory highlights the relevance of circuits in the frontal and parietal lobes that are activated during both attention shifts and subsequent movements.
source_text: the premotor theory highlights the relevance of circuits in the frontal and parietal lobes that are activated during both attention shifts and subsequent movements, so as to strengthen the association process
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the premotor theory based on established literature.

claim: Most of the neurons in the DN exhibit heterogeneous modulations during putative attention shifts and during subsequent goal-directed saccadic eye movements.
source_text: Our data show that most of the neurons in the main output nucleus of the cerebellum, the DN, exhibit heterogeneous modulations during putative attention shifts made when the animals read the peripheral C-stimulus, as well as during the subsequent goal-directed saccadic eye movements that depend on this preceding cue in the peripheral visual field
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the primary findings from the neural recordings.

claim: The converging coordination of cerebellum and cerebral cortex in higher order mental processes such as covert attention also occurs during other cognitive processes.
source_text: The converging coordination of cerebellum and cerebral cortex in higher order mental processes such as covert attention also occurs during other cognitive processes
evidence_reasoning: This is a generalization supported by reference to other cognitive domains.

claim: Not only the mirror neuron system in cerebral cortex but also connected areas in the cerebellum are actively involved in perceiving and interpreting the action of others.
source_text: not only the mirror neuron system in cerebral cortex but also connected areas in the cerebellum are actively involved in perceiving and interpreting the action of others
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to a study on action observation (Abdelgabar et al., 2019).

claim: Lobules VII and VIII in the cerebellar hemispheres are recruited during action observation tasks when evaluating the kinematics of goal-directed hand actions of others.
source_text: just like during the Landolt C task, lobules VII and VIII in the cerebellar hemispheres are recruited during such action observation tasks when evaluating the kinematics of goal-directed hand actions of others
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to a study on action observation (Abdelgabar et al., 2019).

claim: Patients suffering from spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 are severely impaired in performing action observation tasks.
source_text: patients suffering from spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 are severely impaired in performing these tasks
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to a clinical study (Abdelgabar et al., 2019).

claim: Cerebellar processing may help the frontal premotor and parietal cortices to map visual input from high level visual regions onto the motor machinery involved in performing related goal-directed actions.
source_text: One can hypothesize that cerebellar processing helps the frontal premotor and parietal cortices to map visual input from high level visual regions onto the motor machinery involved in performing related goal-directed actions
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly presented as a hypothesis about cerebellar function.

claim: Complex mental observation, either overt or covert, relies on a cortico-cerebellar loop that maps sensory input onto motor control structures (inverse models) and motor programs to expected sensory input (forward models).
source_text: This suggests that much like action control, complex mental observation, either overt or covert, relies on a cortico-cerebellar loop that maps sensory input onto motor control structures (inverse models) and motor programs to expected sensory input (forward models)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation drawing on the internal model framework (Wolpert and Ghahramani, 2000).

claim: The cortico-cerebellar loop brings descending information from visual cortical networks to the cerebellum and ascending information from the cerebellum back to premotor areas in the prefrontal cerebral cortex.
source_text: This loop may bring descending information from our visual cortical networks to the cerebellum and ascending information from the cerebellum back to premotor areas in the prefrontal cerebral cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the directionality of information flow in the cortico-cerebellar loop.

claim: Before being subjected to the peripheral Landolt C saccade task, both animals were used for two other studies.
source_text: Before being subjected to the peripheral Landolt C saccade task of the current study, both of them were used for two other studies, one on glissade control and another one on mechanisms underlying anti-saccades
